utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in the courtroom and those supporting us just outside the courtroom. Madam Registrar would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if it is convenient to the Court, might we interpose Ewa Tabeau at 11.00?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like you to take into account in your scheduling that if any protective measures should be put in place that you do that at least immediately after a relatively long break, because that will take some time. If -- there is no final decision on that because we indicated what the Chamber would like to see and then we got the information that a witness would not be available, so there is no final decision on that. But I think there is no problem to hear Ewa Tabeau, but in the scheduling of time, you should take care that not, for example, start with Ewa Tabeau for quarter of an hour and then immediately go to a witness who is -- who needs half an hour of preparation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I understand. I think that can be avoided, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, sir, I would like to present my apologies to you because we proceeded very slowly yesterday, but it appeared that with reference to some Prosecution documents we did not follow the so-called anti-contamination rule that we normally apply. As to the expert, Mr. Higgs, the Prosecution had asked the expert not to take account of the witness account of the ABC and BC witnesses -- incidents in particular. Now in his report, in certain paragraphs, he refers to them quite extensively --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin I think we gave yesterday the decisions on the admission to evidence. It is your intention to reopen argument on whether these documents should have been admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I believe that that document should be admitted as evidence, but always, according to the usual formula, in order to avoid any contamination as it were, the passages --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are at this moment, reopening --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It would have been proper to ask permission to do so because it is not entirely up to the parties to reopen at any stage a debate which concerns a decision already given. And we will then consider whether such an opportunity will be given or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I do understand that you would like to reopen argument especially, on those parts of the report of Mr. Higgs that relates to the witnesses that have been excluded in the questioning. Yes. Okay, that is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will consider whether an opportunity will be given.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will apologise again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any other procedural issue, if not, Mr. Usher, would you please escort Mr. Gavrankapetanovic into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just while that is happening, again, we have problems with our LiveNote. I wonder whether a technician could attend to it during the evidence, I have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if that would be possible. Mine is functioning, I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Gavrankapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony. Then, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. President. With your leave, Mr. President I would like to show the witness premarked Exhibit P3737 C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: English translation P3737 C.1. They have been premarked so I hope it won't cause the confusion that happened yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just for reference again, the ERN numbers are on every alternate page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Doctor, do you see your signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 02156613, if that is the one you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you see your signature on every page which has numbers on the top right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: For the moment, I would like you to ignore the content of the document. If you could look at the top typed headings, and if you see that there are typed headings and there are handwritten words on top of those typed headings can you explain this to the Court.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If you are referring to the typed headings, it must be the form from a construction company, actually, since the references are to the building worker, the destruction or pulling down of houses. But those typed headings have been crossed, out and then there are handwritten headings in capital letters referring to the name and surname, the place of death.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I may take you back one second. Can you tell the Court which document this is, where does it come from?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This register after the handwritten headings, comes from the morgue of the clinic of the university centre in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is that the morgue at Kosevo Hospital?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I clarified yesterday. There are two names, the one I myself mentioned originally and the other one which is Bonica [phoen] Kosevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. If you can now go through the document and if you could tell the Court whether you see entries for the following dates: The 22nd of January 1994?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The 12th of July 1993?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 12th, the 13th, yes, I can see that. July 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The 1st of June 1993?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the 4th and the 5th of February 1994?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this document correspond to the original that is kept at your institution?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Might that document be removed from the witness. With your leave, Mr. President, I would like to show the witness a final document, it is marked P3737D. English translation, P3737D.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you see your signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And can you read out the name of the person on top of the document?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is 02115962, if that is page 1 the name is Franic Ivan, the year of both is 1930.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. And what type of document is this?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular case, this is a letter of discharge from the abdominal urology department where the patient had been treated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, just in order to avoid whatever confusion, the witness just mentioned the ERN number that is stricken out. I take that it is 02156580. That is the number not stricken out on the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then I have to apologise, yesterday I said that this document would have the same number, but ending at 86, and I said that not similar numbers should be put on documents, but in the subsequent order of numbering of this document, I must have made a mistake yesterday, although it is very difficult to read. It should be eight zero last two digits, instead of what I said yesterday, eight six. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, just for clarification, I cannot see the witness signature. Well, I don't know which of this signatures is that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Maybe the document can be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The one with the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: For the record, the witness points out his signature on the bottom left-hand corner on the first page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Finally, is this document a copy of an original from your institution?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Is -- first, thank you, Mr. Sachdeva. Is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness? Then, please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gavrankapetanovic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 11th of October, 2001, you made a statement to the Prosecution. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, you handed in a certain number of medical files and hospital documents. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "copies" could you tell us whether those files were the ones you selected yourself or whether you were asked to hand in certain types of documents? In other words, what were you asked to hand in?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly what I was asked to do, because I was asked from the service that I am responsible for. It was asked from the staff in charge of the register to hand in certain files and to photocopy them in the presence of the official from the municipal authorities, in this case the centre of Sarajevo where the hospital is situated. So a municipal official was always present and he confirmed that the originals were handed in and then for the first time, these documents were signed by the person who acted as the director of surgical -- of the surgical department. And on all documents, apart from the one relating to the morgue you can see that they bear the signature of that person, followed by my own signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When your service photocopied the originals that you say you have in your possession, can you tell us what files were asked for and with reference to what dates? In other words, were you asked to provide documentation with reference to certain dates and, if so, which ones?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you that because I myself was not in touch with anyone from the Tribunal at the time. I was simply given the documents with reference to which I could tell that they were in line with the originals and so I signed them. And I looked at the dates later.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Okay, Doctor, you are telling us that at the time when you were presented with the medical files from the hospital that you manage, you had no knowledge of the dates that the documents were relating to?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought they asked for documents for the entire period, between 1992 and 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And later on, did you find out from your staff what dates these files referred to?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And what did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was about a couple of dates. Later on when I look at this, I can repeat it was the 31st of May, and the 1st of June 1993, the 12th and the 13th of July 1993, I think it was 20th and 21st of January 1994 and the 4th and 5th of February 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us about the document that you yourself identified as the document listing the names of persons who were supposed to have been injured at Markale.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like Mr. Gavrankapetanovic to be shown the document ERN the last two digits are 6530. It was I believe the first document that my learned colleague submitted yesterday. I think he even referred to the full number, but at this present moment, I can't think of it. The first three -- four digits are 6530. And it was the first document -- it is a typed text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that it was not presented yesterday by the Prosecution, but we will try to retrieve it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour I did get that, because I have two copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You got it, but it has not been tendered. It has been given as a bundle so that we would not need extra time but it has not been presented as far as I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, can you please repeat the ERN number, the beginning and the end number.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 02156530.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And the last number?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have the -- on that page, we have another ERN, the last four digits, 6010, and the very last number on this document is 6032 -- just a minute. 6631.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The easy way of doing it, can you just show us how it looks like to us. Even if you just put it this way so that we can see what it is approximately. Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gavrankapetanovic, you see before you a list which has been typed.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have it on the ELMO so that there is no possible misunderstanding. Mr. Usher, could you then please turn the ELMO so that Mr. Gavrankapetanovic will not twist his -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gavrankapetanovic, could you tell us, please, who made this list?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which number do you mean? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I have before me ERN 6530 in the top of the page?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the top of the document it says "Markale 5th of February 1994." It is 02156530.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that's the one. As much as I can see here, I don't have this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see before you a document which the first page begins with the number 6530?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness's microphone be switched on, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please switch on both microphones of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not the one.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 6536. A six is at the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is not the right number. Mr. Usher, could you please give the whole bundle to the Registrar so that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I can't see 6530. I have 36 here, if that is the one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The bundle will be returned to the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document which the Defence has, 6536, that has the serial number 20. That is the sixth page of the document and the very first page of that bundle is the first page being 6530.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher could you please leave the bundle as it is and put the top page on the -- yes, there we are.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, that is the document which I wanted Mr. Gavrankapetanovic to see.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gavrankapetanovic, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, who wrote on the top of this page "Markale, 5th of February 1994"?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean handwritten?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you that, but I can see that it is written "Markale" and I believe further on with a typewriter, but I can clarify the document. This is one page out of the registration book, the logbook, and it was written in -- it was handwritten, the logbook, and yesterday we were able to see logbook pages which were handwritten. This part which was typed, I presume that the then general manager on that day, that is on the 5th of February 1994, when we are talking about Markale considering that there was an enormous number of dead and wounded, he -- and considering large-scale panic in the city, he, what he had to do, he had to take out from the main logbook only those persons who were injured at Markale market. Taking into account that on that day, just like on any other days, there were injured persons coming from other locations in the city. So what I presumed that happened is that this part was retyped and that it had been posted, had been put on wall, on several occasions in the hospital in front of the mortuary on boards, around the hospital, because there was a lot of panic and there was an interest of the media and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, if we can just clarify this document, who compiled this list?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume this list was compiled by the service, consisting of medical technicians, nurses and other staff, administrative staff, by the order of the general management, so as to announce it publicly who was injured and who died on the 5th of February 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, you are telling us that this document was compiled immediately following 5th of February 1994?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And during the 5th of February 1994, this was a way of informing the public about what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us in the bottom right corner there are two signatures?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You mean whose they are?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had already pointed to my signature, that is the first one, with the date, 11th of January 2002, and the second signature, when we are talking about the name, that is deputy general manager of surgical medicine, who before me, had signed all of the medication -- all of the documentation in relation to the surgical department. And there is also my signature and his in relation to any surgical treatment, except for the mortuary where there is my signature. And this person here is Dr. Emis Solakovic [phoen] he was the deputy. So with my signature, there is also Dr. Solakovic's signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Gavrankapetanovic are you telling us the original of this document, this document consists in your institution?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we keep all the originals.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Specifically this document, which is a copy, does it exist containing the list of other people registered in your logbook?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this was only done when there was mass injury involved. It was in relation to Markale and probably some other incidents, large-scale injuries, which is when relatives, friends, were not able to get in to the clinical centre, the emergency centre because it was practically closed. That is when lists would be put up on different locations, at the centre, so that friends and relatives and others could find out about the names and surnames of those people injured.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor on this document, I will notice on other documents, we can see that it was signed on the 11th of January 2002?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And you told us in your statement of the 11th of October 2001 that you had handed over all the copies?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please clarify?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the very -- to start with, what you asked me to start with, I did not sign a single logbook. It had been signed by the deputy manager of general surgery and this is the signature below. And after that, some two months afterwards, I was asked to sign each one of these documents, which is what I did. And I signed always with a date so that I would know exactly whether I had signed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So what you are telling us, that was on the 11th of February 2002?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No 11th of January 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: 2002. On this document that you see before you, we can see on page one which begins under serial number one, when we see that date and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. hour of admission, we see about 12 hours. Are you confirming that this was typed with a typewriter?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: From number one to number 101, the Defence saw that it says that it was typed-written about 1200 hours and then from 100 to 105 and I believe that would be page which has no ERN number but it comes after 6549 which begins with 101. We can see that on this document the hour of admission is 12.30?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean written in hand?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, could you please explain why is it that here for 100 numbers, 100 patients it was typed about 12 and then it was written in hand?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the main logbook that we saw in fact in its copy which was properly certificated and signed, you can see that hour of admission was 12.35. These patients certainly could not come within 60 seconds, but they did come in very quick succession. This time around 12.00, this is when we put an approximate time, so it could have been 11.30, it could have been 12.35. And somebody had added that it was -- that it was on that day, on the 2nd of February, somebody had added 12.35. It was impossible to admit 50, 60 people in one minute, but then of course, considering that the passage to the hospital was also blocked because of all the injured and all the cars, they may have come within 20 minutes of each other, all of those who were going to the emergency centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask if the doctor can be shown document ERN 6568 -- 6586. Not that document, but another document, the last four digits being 6586 of the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Do you have the exhibit number, Ms. Pilipovic, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that my colleagues had a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it from the same batch we received -- yes, there we are.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we received that yesterday and I believe that --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document number P3737A.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, you explained to us yesterday that this is a logbook where upon admission in hospital, certain data is entered and that this data is entered by the nurses?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said was that names and surnames and possibly people who escorted them and the date of birth, if the person is employed and so on, this is done by the nurses. But the diagnosis is done by the doctors.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Doctor, could you please look at this document and show us from which serial number victims were brought in from Markale?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is the document we are talking, P3737A, is that the document we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: That is the document that you see before you, and begins with the page 6586.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Fine. That is the very last patient on the page. His name is Muagic [phoen], date of birth 1957, address Slavje Cavena Tutra [phoen] Street number 6, which is where he lived. The name cannot be read.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us before the name, could you tell us the date?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very difficult to see, but it is 7/05.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So that is the first one?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These two patients arrived on the same day. That is, four patients came, but they were injured on other locations. I am talking from midnight after 5th of February.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you are talking about other locations, Doctor, could you please tell us whether in this logbook, we have a column where we can see from which location a patient was brought in?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is -- this is admissions of patients into the centre. Sometimes we had the address of the patient, where he comes from, and sometimes the location where he had come from.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I understand, you told us that the data is inputted by the nurse and diagnosis by the doctor?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who takes the anamnesis from the patient?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is done by the doctor, if the patient is conscious, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Now, if the patient is conscious, on the basis of what the patient says, does then the doctor establish the diagnosis, whether that is the right diagnosis?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. The diagnosis is what happens after the doctor has checked him. The previous, the anamnesis could be speaking technically medically, that could be half of the diagnosis, but it is only after a thorough examination that it can -- something else can be said.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Now, that when you tell us that this is the logbook of the hospital, you are confirming that the original of this document exists in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many persons were brought in on the 5th of February 1994 who were dead on arrival?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you on the top of my head, but I am sure we do have this data.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The Defence examined this document carefully and on page 6594 we saw that there were six people on the 5th of February.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean from number 790?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. By carefully examining this logbook for numbers from 705 to 797 in relation to the 5th of February, we have it marked that there are six people?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this page, there are more than six, but I don't know which six you mean. You mean six dead?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing that you can make a distinction here, if you allow me and that is, according to our documentation, three persons, the first three diagnosis, we have the names, but I am not going to give them to you, that people died, people were killed outside. Motis Alatis [pheon], the doctor confirmed diagnosis, the definite diagnosis that death occurred on the way to the hospital, which is that the patient was dead on arrival. This is the case with three patients and the following two patients, X, Y, that is a man and he was looked at, he was taken to thoracic surgery, and this is when he died. The following two patients were taken to the operation theatre and both of them died during surgery, either during preparatory proceedings or when they started -- tried to stop them bleeding. But unfortunately they both died during surgery.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Doctor, we agree that in this logbook that is from your institution, we can see that six people died who were brought in on the 5th of February 1994 and for whom you told us that these persons had been brought from Markale, as it was written in your logbook?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, you are only speaking about one page. If you wish to do this, we can go through all the page. I am prepared to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I agree. Perhaps I wasn't careful enough. So from number 705.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 888. 888, 889, would be the following number as well, except that with the first patient, death occurred at the intensive care unit and the second one was -- died outside. There are two -- other two logbooks, the logbook of the operations theatre, which correlates fully with the logbook that we see here. And then there is a second logbook, logbook of the morgue, or the mortuary, where the dead were taken directly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Doctor, but I only asked you about the logbook from your institution, the one we see before you, where I saw -- you said that there was another person?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another two people.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Another two people, that would be eight persons, about whom you stated that these people had died in your institution, and they were brought on the 2nd of February.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are talking about people who died on the same date, 5th of February. And we are talking about the people who were brought to the emergency centre, and death occurred, and was recorded in the logbook. There are different logbooks but the two are most significant, rather three are most significant, I mentioned one which is the logbook of the operations, the surgical procedures, and then the second one of the intensive care unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor --

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the third one, the most important one is the logbook of the morgue, of the mortuary.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So are you telling us, Doctor, that in this document that we see before us there is actually a proper content, a list of people who were brought on the 5th of February to your hospital?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned yesterday, if you were listening, that there were three institutions in the city of Sarajevo, which is the Dobrinja hospital, probably because of its location could not admit many injured from the 5th of February. And the second institution is the general hospital which was able to admit a large number of injured. And the third one is ours, and they admitted most of the patients.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that, Doctor, but to start with you told us that this text which was typed with a typewriter, for the 5th of February, it was established that there were 127 people and that it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic speed is going astronomical at this moment. Could you please slow down. And you also, Dr. Gavrankapetanovic, slow down, otherwise, the interpreters will not be able to follow you. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Gavrankapetanovic, the first document I submitted to you, 6530, that we were looking at, and with reference to which we agreed that it is report from your hospital, that you yourself signed on the date of the 5th of February 1994, it is a typed written text and it ends with a number 127. And it refers to persons injured or killed at the Markale square according to your evidence. You also told us that it was compiled on the basis of the hospital register. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was compiled on the basis of the company registers, in the plural.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So we do agree that this document submitted to the Prosecution does not represent actual state of affairs on that day, the 5th of February 1994?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have to include something which is rather significant, if you allow me to complement this idea. We have to refer to the register of the morgue, which is separate, because that is the place where the dead were taken directly. I mean all those people that displayed certain signs of death were taken there directly. There was no need for taking them to the emergency. So they were taken directly to the morgue, which is also part of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, will you agree with me that the first document we were looking at, the typed written one, 6530 is the document which was drawn up much later than the day we were referring to originally, the 5th of February, that it might have been drawn up subsequently?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was signed later, but I can't tell you that it was compiled later.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you can't tell us exactly on what day it was drawn up?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was certainly drawn up on that day. I did mention that I was not a part of the management of the hospital at the time, but I know for certain that the lists were displayed on a number of locations throughout the hospital so that the people could find out, I mean, the family and friends, could find out who had been injured or who, unfortunately, had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: But, Doctor, you can agree with me that it is a document coming from your hospital?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So the staff of your hospital compiled this list of names at your hospital?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that that list of names is not in line with your actual hospital register which refers to the admissions of all patients entering the hospital, could you then explain the differences between the two documents?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We have thirty-six organisational units as we call them, fifteen surgical departments. Every surgical department, and that's what we are talking about, has a separate register.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, does it mean that the name of one and the same patient can be found more than once in all the various registers, if the patient is moved from one department, one ward to the other?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But just let me add, all those who are only lightly injured, those bearing isolated injuries, there was no need for them to be sent to the emergencies. We then redistributed patients, so to say, and sent them to other wards. And basically, what we were looking at here were only one or two units, that is to say the operating theatre and C-3. They were redistributed to other clinical wards for various injuries -- injuries to the senses or injuries to their extremities, et cetera. But, of course, all those who were severely injured, were listed in this protocol.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, can you tell us whether for all these people whose names can be found in this list, there is a case history as well?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us with reference to the patients admitted to your hospital whether you had them X-rayed?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Due to the speed of the operations and the flow of people, unfortunately, at that particular time we were unable to have all the patients X-rayed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us on the basis of what you entered the data about the causes of the injuries?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The admissions were managed by the most senior surgeon on call, the most experienced person on the staff. And believe me, if there is somebody who comes along and their leg has been chopped off, you can tell what happened even without an X-ray, and the same refers to punctured lungs or open head injuries, their insides spilling out, I mean, you can tell it with the naked eye, you don't have to have them X-rayed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I can agree with that statement. But can you explain to us how you can tell without an X-ray that it was a sniper injury or rather can you tell us on the basis of what you could tell that it was a sniper wound?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really know what case you are referring to in particular, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I am going to submit to you a paper --

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have the so-called high nozzle velocity injury which means injuries caused by high speed bullets and the entry and exit points can tell you that we are talking about a high energy bullet. High impact bullet. As to whether it is an artillery piece causing that or other weapons with a low initial speed such as various guns or whether these wounds caused by shrapnel from shells, they appear, they have a specific type of appearance. I can't explain it right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: All I was asking you about, was the people who had sniper wounds, since in the document that the Prosecution has, there is this reference to snipers. That was all I was asking you about. Do you draw these conclusions on the basis of the statements made by the patients themselves, on the basis of the data they provide when you decide on the diagnosis, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has to do with the way in which the wound has penetrated the soft tissue. There you hardly need -- I mean, I am talking about high impact wounds. You hardly need an X-ray there because you will open the wound -- I mean, the surgeon will open the wound and will be able to tell, as opposed to wounds of bone structure, where X-rays are necessary, of course, if you have the opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can a surgeon, when examining a patient, tell whether the wound was caused by sniper or by a gun bullet?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He can tell whether it was a high or low impact bullet.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, can you tell us whether at your hospital when it comes to the patients who died in the course of their treatment, whether you carried out any post-mortems?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In all cases where there was suspicious death we asked for forensic examination to be carried out. Very rarely we had highly specialised pathological post-mortems. But considering the extremely high number of casualties, especially during a certain period, it was not possible to carry out those post-mortems so the dead in order to prevent any outbreaks of infection, were buried, as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What I am referring to in particular is the incident that we have discussed at greatest length, on the 5th of February 1994. And then the incident which happened on the 1st of June and the 12th of July. In those cases, did you carry out any post-mortems?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something which is within the area of the competence of the faculty of medicine and it is outside the scope of what the hospital does. And two people who were employed at the centre simply did not have time, physically to carry out all the post-mortems, and therefore, except in very rare cases, we did not carry out the post-mortems.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, are you telling us that during that particular period of time, in 1992, 1993, 1994, you did not carry out post-mortems or in other words that your hospital does not have any documents referring to these post-mortems?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am going to repeat my answer. Legal medicine is a discipline which is within the area of the competence of the faculty of medicine, and therefore the hospital does not make any decisions as to what patients are going to be submitted for post-mortems. We can only make suggestions. In all cases where there was even a slight suspicion as to the cause of death we always requested a post-mortem. As to whether those post-mortems were carried out by the competent professionals, I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, you are telling us that you, yourself have no knowledge about whether these post-mortems had been carried out or not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it really necessary to hear the answers to similar questions three, four, five times? I think the witness has been quite clear on this issue. So if there is any additional information you would like to hear ask the witness, but do not repeat your questions or seek confirmation of the answers already given once or twice. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. But I don't think I have received a satisfactory answer as to the fact that Mr. Gavrankapetanovic has no knowledge of these post-mortems. It did not seem like a clear answer and that is why I insisted?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, can you explain to us, when you talk about a case history of disease, does it always have to be recorded on a relevant form?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you have such a form.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is that form an integral part or rather, if we talk about a case history, does it normally include the letter of discharge at the end?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Page 1 is basically the part or rather the copy of the first page is the part that is given to the patient or the document that we give to our patients when they are released from hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, so when a patient is discharged, they get a letter of discharge?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I have misunderstood you. Is that letter of discharge an integral part of the case history, the very same form, is it a different form? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The case history, or the anamnesis refers to at least four pages and the letter of discharge can only include two pages, or rather, a sheet of paper. In the case history, two pages are connected. You can sort of leaf through them as if it were a book. If a patient had spent a long time at the hospital, you can have as many as eight or even more pages. And the letter of discharge is always a single page, possibly two, and if there is a long text, you write on the second page, but generally speaking, it is just one page.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: From what I have gathered, you confirm that in 1992, 1993, 1994, you worked at the clinical centre?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, throughout that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether your hospital admitted soldiers as well?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to us, upon admission of soldiers what did you enter into your files, on the basis of what did you say that those were soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the technical and administrative staff who were in charge of that. You refer to the name and surname of the patient, the year of their birth, the place from where they were brought to the hospital, and possibly their address, and if they were soldiers or a member of the police force, their unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, may I ask you, you used now the same time as has been used in chief. May I take it that you will finish in a couple of minutes? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, have I understood you correctly in that these persons, soldiers and police officers, when it comes to the files kept at your hospital had been entered into these files in a separate way?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was only entered in to the general register. But we indicated that there were soldiers, in other words, everybody admitted to the hospital, either due to illness or injury, their names were entered into the register, no matter they were soldiers, police officers, civilians, children, women, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, can you answer just one more question: Considering that we have heard quite a few witness accounts about many people being members of the BH army and not wearing uniforms, when it came to these people when they were brought to your hospital, if they were injured or wounded in any way, on the basis of what did you determine their status?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, soldiers were mostly in uniforms. If there Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. were some discrepancies -- and that only referred to the very beginning of the war. But even if they did not wear a full uniform, normally we could tell that they were members of the army because they had some insignia.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. THE COURT: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Sachdeva, is there any need to --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- re-examine the witness? Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Can the witness be shown Exhibit P3737C.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which number, sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Doctor, can you please go to -- firstly to the page with the reference number 02156620. On the right hand, right corner at the bottom is number 92.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, if you can go to the next page. I have to do it this way, because the next page is not referred to by numbers. Perhaps you can put the document on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is too big. I don't know if it will fit the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can it be moved to the right a little bit, please. Yes, keep going the other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: On the column on the left, can you see the figure 316?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the next row after that, can you explain what is filled in in those rows?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am going to have to repeat what I have already said, that is to say, that this form comes from a construction company because you can see that it refers to the type of machinery used, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: It was my fault. I wasn't precise enough. I am talking about the columns underneath the heading -- the columns with the typed headings, where the name is there, you can see Mida Gonovic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Yes, I do see it. The register had been rewritten, as it were, because we -- there was a shortage of paper, a shortage of registers. And so this is the register from the morgue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you see the word "Markale"?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And can you explain what that means?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the names of the dead brought from Markale and the serial number, the first one is 316 and the last one is 330 on the 5th of February, their identification in terms of identifying who they were, the names, the address, and name of their parents was not entered, but we have sex, male or female.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So this page shows that everyone, all these people were brought in directly from Markale to the morgue on this page?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you move two pages forward, now. You should have 331 on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is it the same for this page? This page shows people were brought in from Markale?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, starting with 331, through to 345, the date is the 5th of February 1994, and the place of injury, rather the place of death, in this case, I apologise, Markale. Sex, male or female, and we don't have the name of the father and the address Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. And now a further two pages forward, starting from the number 346 on the left-hand side. It can be moved slightly -- that is correct.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a difference here. All these people were dead between 346 and 360, the ones that were taken directly to the morgue from Markale are the numbers from 346 through to 353, the late Mrs. Smilja Delic [phoen] from Markale. And 354 through to 360 where patients who actually died at the neurosurgical ward.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. Last question: Do you know people were taken to other hospitals on the 5th of February 1994 from Markale in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, if we refer to any other hospitals, some people were taken to the general hospital of Sarajevo, and I did already reply to Mrs. Pilipovic that we have 15 surgical wards, departments, within the clinical centre which could deal with some isolated injuries without the need for people to be taken to the emergencies first.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Were there any cases for medical insurance, if the patient was a soldier or a dependent of a soldier?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no insurance for anyone. It was a free for all. We did not get paid anyway. There was no taxation, there was nothing whatsoever, so everybody was treated in the same way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transport, there is an inversion of the question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That concludes the re-examination, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sachdeva. Before adjourning may I just ask you, what will be the order after the break and if there -- if it would be needed, prepare for protective measures I would rather finish now --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I think it is -- indeed I think it is likely at this stage that we won't need those measures from first thing tomorrow. When one factors in the time required for Ewa Tabeau and Mrs. Arifagic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will now have a break. Mr. Gavrankapetanovic, there might be one or more questions from the Bench, so we will adjourn until 5 minutes past 11.00 and your presence is still required at that moment. We will adjourn until 5 minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi has one or more questions to you, Mr. Gavrankapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] Sir, I would like to show you some documents. Madam Registrar, could you help me, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document P3737A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir could you please have a look at number 777. If I understand correctly, the hour of admission is 1545, and then 778 is 1235 hours. And if you have a look at further down to 795, the hour of admission is 1620 hours. And then the name which appears before and after, the hour of admission is 1235. Could you perhaps explain to us this phenomena, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have seen that from one area in the city, more than 100 injured persons were admitted but their treatment lasted for several hours. For some of them you were able to see, even here at the end, the end of this part that you mentioned, they don't even sometimes have name and surname, when we are talking about Markale. But they were admitted as X, Y, either as a male or female person. For the two cases that you mentioned, they did not come from the Markale area. Mr. Hodzic was injured in Hrsanica so he did not come from Markale and his hour of admission was inputted and the second person, Mr. Keso also from another location, not from Markale, we took care of both persons, but we set them apart from the people injured in Markale, and that is where we put that they were admitted at 1235 hours. That means that for these two people, this is to say that they were not in the same group injured with the group in Markale. Just like those people who were injured up to 1000 hours, and those who were injured late at night, they came from other locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand what you are saying but what surprises me a little is that afterwards, the hour of admission is 1235. So for 777 the hour of admission was 1445 and then you took the injured from the Markale market? It is this phenomenon which made me look at it more closely, and that is why I ask for your clarification.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All the people were admitted from Markale and they were all located in one place, and that is for this reason, is that we also had some people who were injured the same period around about the Markale incident. They were also admitted and we also had to take care of them. That was our duty. Now, the fact is that there were probably not all people were entered, those who arrived. They were probably not put into the registration book immediately. But, first of all, they were treated, surgically treated, the bleeding was stopped, their wounds were attended to, and then possibly they were entered into the registration book, into the logbook, because it was probably impossible to do it properly, so that it would be properly visible for all the people that arrived at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Gavrankapetanovic, this concludes your testimony in this court -- but Ms. Pilipovic is standing so let me just first hear what she would like to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The question that I would like to ask comes from a question that was asked by Judge El Mahdi. And Dr. Gavrankapetanovic clarified for Mr. Fikret Hodzic, what happened, that the person who was injured in Hrasnica, if I understood the doctor correctly, and the time for that was 1545 hours. And my question in relation to document 6530, this was the first document which was typed document, according to the testimony of the doctor, the persons who were injured in Markale and the number 83 in this document this is an English translation, page is 2527, 2527, under number 83. I am trying to be able to read in this document which is not very legible. I am trying to find it in B/C/S so that I can read it. But I cannot find it. However, in the translation of this document, in the translation of this document, and Yes, I have found it in the B/C/S version 6544 or page 6020.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you see, Doctor, and the number 83, it's not that document you need the document -- the very first document we looked at, the typed document ERN 6530. Last four digits.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, is this going to get a "D" number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the question is, whether this -- this was in the bundle, and you, for the first time, gave it to the witness. Are you going to tender that and that would then be number D --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And may I take it that the translation will then be D171.1 yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, could you please look at page 6544. Serial number 83. 6544. Number 83, can you see it?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, you told us that this document was compiled including all the people who were injured in Markale, in accordance with the registration in your service, and following Judge El Mahdi's question, for the person under 777, Mr. Fikret Hodzic who was injured and received at 1545, you said he was injured in Hrasnica. How can you explain that this person, Fikret Hodzic appears on this list to be this person who was injured at Markale?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the service that had the task of retyping all the names of people injured on that day -- did this and they went, according to the logbook, to the registration hospital book, in the main logbook, which was handwritten. So it happened that this person also appeared on this list, but the main registration book, the main logbook of the emergency centre which was handwritten it is obvious that this is the registration book which is the most authentic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that was my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. Then, Dr. Gavrankapetanovic, I repeat that this concludes your testimony in this court. I thank you very much for having come to The Hague and that you have given answers to all the questions of both parties and of the Bench. And I wish you a good trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Mr. President. I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please escort Mr. Gavrankapetanovic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you please assist us in going through the documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3737A, extract from the records of the Sarajevo clinical reception in Triasbloc [phoen] in B/C/S; P3737A.1, English translation; P3737B, extract from the record of the operating room of surgical clinics in B/C/S; P3737B.1, English translation; P3737C, medical documentation excerpt from logbook in B/C/S; P3737C.1, English translation; P3737D, medical documentation; P3737D.1 English translation -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence objects to the admission of these documents into evidence. We believe that these are not authentic documents. We don't think that the copies are authentic copies of originals. I believe that we think that these documents have been manipulated and that they were compiled after certain events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What documents are you now talking about? The last --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am talking about 3737A, which is the very first document. I am talking about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: B and C?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 3737B and 3737C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say that the Defence is of the opinion that these are manipulated documents. Is there any further explanation to that?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, from the very first moment, the Defence contested the authenticity of the medical documentation because it was barely legible and because it was impossible to tender originals before the Chamber and the Defence in order to prove the authenticity of the documents, which is why we stand by objections regarding the medical documentation, which was disclosed by the Prosecution to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I now hear several different arguments. First -- your first explanation was that these were manipulated. Then I heard that they were badly legible. And so is it the manipulation at this moment? I mean, and where do we find here the bad legibility, because that has been an issue very often. And, of course, we see that there are some handwritten parts.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am just trying to understand your objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, specifically, when we are looking at document 3737C, from this document it is so illegible that we can't even make out which institution it is, if it does relate to a medical institution at all. Specifically, the stamp, the seal is barely visible. We cannot see which institution is in question. Particularly because the -- what the witness said and we are also believe -- we have suspicions that this document had been compiled after the fact. I cannot see a seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Am I correct I heard no questions about seals or the witness has testified that this comes from his hospital, from, I think, C is from the morgue of the hospital. I have not heard any question that would put in dispute that fact. So I am just wondering, I am trying to understand your objection, and I am also trying to put that objection in its procedural context. But let's hear what it Prosecution has to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I also believe that the witness has testified in court to the authenticity of these documents, and for each of the documents that have been shown to him, he has confirmed that they emanate from his institution, an institution which he is the director general of. The issue of manipulation has not been put directly to the witness, and so I would submit that these documents should be admitted into evidence. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. The documents are admitted into evidence. Then we were, Madam Registrar, at P3737D, I think. Because the objection was about 3737 A, B, and C. Or would the objection also relate to "D"? No. So we then have P3737D.1 --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Your Honour, I am just trying to identify the 3737D document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is the Franic medical record. The four page --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes. That was also an objection to the Defence and the witness explained what the medical history was and what was a letter of discharge because we had two different documents from Mr. Franic but the document, which is in form of a letter of discharge, was illegible at the time when we had it. That was 5477. And later on, the Defence received a document which was more legible, but only its case history and not a letter of discharge. So we object to the letter of discharge as being illegible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What part can't you read Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that is the section in the middle. I am talking about document 2477. This is the letter of discharge of Mr. Franic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am talking about P3737D. And that is the -- I think that is what has been tendered now by the Prosecution. So we have to decide on the admission of that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is the document 3737D, then that is the case history as much as I can see from the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, the Defence has now objection as regards the legibility, since it is a legible document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I then may conclude that there are no objections against P3737D and there is no other document in respect of Mr. Franic that is tendered at this moment? Am I right in understanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I recall there was one document that was tendered during the testimony in respect to that incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have to -- it is rather about a patient than about an incident, I think. Madam Registrar would there be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At earlier stages, there has been a dispute about the legibility of the discharge letter of Mr. Franic. It was my understanding that rather than putting into evidence the information contained in the discharge letter, you now relied upon the medical record of the hospital. But if that is wrong, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you are tendering now P3737D?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's then admitted in evidence. Then we have two Defence documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D171, medical documentation; Exhibit D171.1, English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I hear no objections so therefore they are admitted into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Mr. Stamp, perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, the next witness will be Ewa Tabeau --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ewa Tabeau --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And she is here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and the Defence has requested to cross-examine the witness on the additional part of her report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: May I be excused, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you are. Do you have copies to be tendered or -- I know that the additional part of the report has been filed with the Registry.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I must confess that the document having been prepared at the request of the court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- and having been filed not to us or not by us but through the Registry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- I would have thought that it went automatically as an addendum without us having to make a formal application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I -- first of all, I do agree that it was the request of the court and part of the confirmation contained in it was in request of the Defence, because the Defence added a few aspects. So then you -- Mr. Usher, could you then please bring in Ewa Tabeau. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you to leave the courtroom for one more second, yes. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was going to say I have only communicated in sign language with the Prosecution recently because we simply received a couple of pieces of paper for a witness who is going to come soon, but then these photocopies are really not legible. If you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. could provide us with more legible documentation during the course of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that during the last break you showed it to the Prosecution and they refused --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have only just received them and I have tried to communicate my complaint in sign language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this a document that will be used during the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It is, Mr. President. And we have the original copy here for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is just as dark as the --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There are parts of it which are not completely legible. My understanding is that the relevant part, the part which is relevant to the issue in this case is legible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Let's then see. So I do understand that the Prosecution has no better legible copies available for the Defence. Okay, that -- having established that, could we then please ask Mr. Usher to escort Ms. Tabeau into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I was wondering if the Court was indicating that perhaps I could assist the Court with copies?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I left my copy on my desk. I studied it yesterday evening, but I left it on my desk, but my colleagues might have been more -- they have copies. Please be seated, Ms. Tabeau. We are being very impolite not saying good morning to you and not asking you to be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I apologise for that. But we are still trying to get distributed your last part of the report that has been distributed before, but is not in everyone's hand at this moment. Mr. Usher, would you please. Ms. Tabeau, may I first thank you for your quick reply to the request of the Chamber to provide additional information and I take it that I can also speak on behalf of the Defence that asked for specific information as well. The Defence has asked to put additional questions to you in relation to this additional document. May I take it, Mr. Stamp, that since you have not expressed such a wish, that you have no questions at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Good day, Mrs. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration hat you gave at the very beginning of your testimony. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for being here. Thank you for having come so swiftly and for having done all this fast, perhaps a bit too fast. Can you confirm the report that you have drawn up? It is not dated, by the way.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: It is not dated? I think it is dated here. The 24th of July. This is what I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. It is dated, but it is not signed. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps for the record, if the copy in the hands of the Registrar will be given to the witness so that she can identify this document as the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
