utterances.text: Thank you. Mrs. Tabeau, it is a three-page document, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps, Ms. Tabeau, if you keep the document that you just identified, that is the document we will now use in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. President, perhaps I could ask the witness to sign this document which can be then tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Mrs. Tabeau, you have looked at the losses, that is to say, those killed and those wounded and you found that the overall figure was lower than your initial figure. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: You are speaking now about table 3, I believe?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am making a general statement, Madam, and with reference to table 3, but the result is included in your table 3. Let me just specify that we don't have enough time so let me just ask you, yes or no, did you find that the number of victims was lower or not?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot answer this type of question. We were discussing 6.055 records last time from table 2, and you suggested that approximately 2000 of records from this total, I am speaking about killed persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Let me stop you here. Is it not correct, Madam, representative of the Prosecution, that in the column included in table 3, there is a difference of the order of 10.456.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I want to know if it is appropriate to address the witness as Madam, representative of the Prosecution. That is an argument which is a matter that we can ventilate elsewhere. If he could refer to her as Dr. Tabeau or Madam Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see before that on the names that you give to your submissions, you are even commenting on the titles of your submissions. In this Tribunal, there are witnesses, there are expert witnesses, and it is fully inappropriate once some person is examined as a witness or an as expert witness to refer to such a witness or expert witness as a representative of the Prosecution. You could have known this, you should have known this. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, very much, Mr. President. Well, I would like you to assist me because the witness refuses to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You interrupted her when she was answering a question. Would you please put a clear question to the witness. It is not the feeling of this Chamber that this expert witness refuses to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is it correct, Madam - and I would be very grateful if you could answer by a yes or no - that having revised your calculations, you found that the overall number of victims was lower; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. It is -- I revised the figure you were discussing last time, you were interested in the numbers of excluded records that were still relevant to the area within confrontation lines and were related to the whole period covered by this study. So I have this number and this number is mentioned in table 3, column 3 --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: May I interrupt you, Madam. You said "no" so did you find that the overall number was higher?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: The overall number reported in my study, the number of killed persons and wounded persons, related to the indictment period and indictment area remained the same. This has not changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, Madam --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we are wasting time because I believe that the witness does not wish to give a precise answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, let me by quite clear. You put a question to the witness and you said "answer by yes or no." The first word of her answer was "no" and then she tried to explain why and then you interrupted her halfway. So there is no way of saying that if you are interested to hear an explanation, ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is it correct, Madam, yes or no, that there is a difference of the order of 370 killed and one thousand and more wounded --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the last figure, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This number that you mentioned is indeed used to correct figures --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: That is not my question, Madam. My question is simply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I want you to treat this expert witness in a polite way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam witness, you have understand my question very well. The question refers to specific figures. Yes or no, is there a difference of the order of 317 with respect to the killed and 1.667 for the wounded; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I object. Counsel cannot insist on a yes or no answer without a simple well defined question, clear and simple. The question is too vague for a yes or no answer. Any answer from an expert would require qualification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Tabeau if a yes or no answer could not be given, the Chamber would like to hear what your answer to the question is. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I haven't had the opportunity to reply to the objection. I would like this to be taken note of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Let me rephrase my question and I will take all the time I need, otherwise, I will ask for it to be noted that we will be renouncing our rights considering the quality of the replies. Well, mathematically speaking, is there a difference that I am referring to, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, mathematically speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. President, my question was clear and it took me five minutes to obtain an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I am not going to grant any extra time on the basis of what happened the last five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is it correct, Madam, that in your table 3, you have included the new changes in the third column, 3, new column; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a new column.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you included the new figures then; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, these are new figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. These new figures are based on the fact that you have subtracted from the overall period, taking into consideration the elements which should not have been included due to either the places or the locations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: The substraction is indeed related to places and dates that were unknown, reported unknown.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If you could just please answer yes or no, we would gain some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I allowed witness to give explanations, if she thinks that a yes or no could not be given. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you have taken into consideration these elements; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Unknown dates, unknown places, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You have subtracted figures with reference to column 3 and 4; is that correct, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And that column gives you a result at the end of it, that's the column referring to the difference, is that correct, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: The difference is the difference --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And you have indicated in your text below your report that the difference referred to the period of time, basically, between January and September 1992, basically, the 9th of September 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: And also including the period in August 1994 and September 1994 that are outside the indictment period.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: On the other hand, in order to carry out this entire operation, you included into column 4, subtitle replicated, exactly the same figures as the one included in your previous report, is that correct, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: These columns are replicated, yes, in the same table.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: That was not really my question. That was not my question. I am referring to column 4. You have included exactly the same figures as the ones included in your previous analysis; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, column 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: That would mean, Madam that you considered that there was no case that could have been excluded due to elements referring to time or place in this last column, so that is why you reported as it was before; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Column 4 includes only records that are known, specific, in terms of dates and places. The records unknown, unknown places were excluded from column 4 from the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, is it correct, that in the last analysis, you did not exclude from your report due to unknown data, things referring to the period of time before September 1992; is that so, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Column 2 indeed included unknown dates and places.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, no. Column 2 included unknown places, but not column 4?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Not column 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So how come column 4 does not include item -- in column 4 they are included?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: In column 4 unknown places and dates are excluded and not included. Unknown dates and unknown places are excluded from column 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, is it not true that column 2 included some errors and how come, if that was the case, there were no errors in column 4?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether we can speak about errors. It is that I never explained in the report the meaning of column 2. So we cannot speak about errors. We --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, but this is a point of methodology. It would mean that in the report there was the inclusion of persons or cases which should not have been included for reasons of time and place; is that true?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: I am sorry. Would you please repeat your question because I didn't understand your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, in terms of methodology, the work that you have carried out is based on the fact that in your previous report there were certain cases referring to situations which should not have been included due to reasons of time and place. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: In our first report, not the addendum that we made now, we discussed numbers that were adjusted from unknown places and dates. There were no unknown places and that included in the figures I reported in this study. However, table 2 was a general overview of survey material. So there are different types of information in this table in our report. We first reported all number, all records that were obtained in the very beginning and then we reported, sort of intermediate step - this is column 2 from table 2 - and in the end, we reported the numbers that are directly relevant to the indictment period and indictment area. And these numbers were discussed in the rest of the report. These numbers don't include unknown dates, unknown places.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, Madam. I quite understand that. But in your report, number one, you had column 2 of table 2, which apparently was wrong. Is that correct? Let's put it in another way, which included figures which were too high?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: From the point of view of the indictment period, indictment area, yes, column two includes numbers that are too high. But I don't discuss these numbers in our report. We only mentioned these numbers to give you some impression about how many records were excluded and for what reasons. And in my addendum, I am even more specific about excluded records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you are interested to ask questions also about the part the Defence specifically asked for, I indicate to you now that you used approximately 20 minutes that was the maximum time you asked yesterday, for questioning this witness. So you have three minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, just very briefly, how come there have not been such errors in the column, the last column of table 3 in your first report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The question includes a statement of something which the witness has not accepted and is not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I withdraw the question. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is it correct that a part of -- one and a quarter of victims were injured or killed in the first period, the first 3 months of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: The number is 7.085, this is the number of wounded persons who were wounded in the -- outside the indictment period.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could you assist me in finally obtaining the answer to this kind question that I have asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I earlier said that clear answers -- clear questions give clear answers. I could add to that that politely put answers give -- questions give perhaps the answers. But Madam Tabeau, I think that Mr. Piletta-Zanin would like to know what part of the injuries and the people killed took place in the first period, compared to the other part of the conflict where he was not very precise, but you perhaps could give us this precision, whether the other part relates only to the period of the indictment or to the period of the whole conflict. So what percentage of injuries and casualties took place in this first four months compared the remaining month of the conflict or the indictment period. And I think an approximate answer does not necessarily have to be three digits after the column.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We need to compare two figures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Figure for wounded persons, 20.004. From column 3, new. And figure 7.085. The 7.085 records are records that are unrelated to the indictment period and indictment area. So a quarter, your approximation, is almost correct. This even, I believe, more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if there is any last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, to the extent that your figures were rectified downwards and there have been changes in the meantime, is it not true that all your conclusions are relatively -- I mean, in a relative fashion, influenced by these changes and that more specifically with reference to the rates that you have determined; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, in fact, at all. Because the correction was made in regard to the records excluded and not included in my study. So the numbers presented in the demographic report that I submitted originally are all correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, the rate -- the rate -- the rate of deaths, for instance, is correct, at the very same time when you are stating that there were fewer deaths than what you have put in your previous report. Is that how I should understand this?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am trying not to object --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's just see --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Same objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I answer this question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please. If you want to reread it on your Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I read it again. The correction I made is related to the excluded records, records that were not analysed in our demographic report. So the rates presented in the report remain the same. And the rates you have here in your report are also correct. Because there are no specific dates and places in these rates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I indicated that that would be your final question. Mr. Stamp, would there be any need to re-examine the witness on the basis of the further questions? Judge Nieto-Navia has one or more questions to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just to put things in summary. I understand you well, replicated column 1 is the same column 1 of the former table 2?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Replicated column 2 is the same column 2 of the former table 2?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Replicated column 4 is the same column 3 of the former table 2?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. It is column 3, former table 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Yes. So the changes are between the new column 2 and the -- well, the new 3 is the correction to the former column 2?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Column 4, former column 3, doesn't change?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Doesn't change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: No further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since neither Judge El Mahdi nor I myself have any further questions to you, Ms. Tabeau, this concludes your examination -- I said this before, but this was not the final conclusion. You are now excused and I thank you for having come back to this courtroom. Mr. Usher, would you please escort Ms. Tabeau out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could the copy that you used be returned to the Registrar. [The witness withdrew]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From a technical point of view, I think the document should be considered as being part of the report and the document has been identified. Madam Registrar, what would be the best way of giving it a number or and then what number or just -- perhaps you should find a number which relates to the report itself and then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This addendum which has been drafted on the request of the Chamber, including the request from the Defence, will have Exhibit number 3731C. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, for the transcript, the Defence would like to state the offending of the rights and would like to state, if you will allow me, that in relation to page 54 line 9, I would have asked a question -- it seemed that I would have asked questions which were not polite, which is not true. The Defence never lacked any courtesy or politeness for the simple reason, we did not call the witness representative of the Prosecution, which she is. But we would like to say that we were very destabilised here seriously destabilised here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What were the words that you used, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if it were not representative of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 54 line 9, I have simply asked, I believe my system has been blocked, so like many others, what I said was not in any case impolite or lacking in courtesy. If I have asked to be given "yes or no" answers regarding the figures, this is in order to save time, and not to be impolite. And I reiterate, that, therefore, I believe that I have a right to state that the rights of the Defence have been offended because the Court -- the Chamber had said it in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please assist me. I have difficulty in finding again your response to your objection, Mr. Stamp, or if -- we know that we all have difficulties with LiveNote today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you can find it in 54.9. My question was the following: "Apart of one and half of the victims were injured or killed in the first period, the first 3 months of the conflict."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am seeking where I responded --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And just below -- just above, just below, below, line 17, you add this following: [In English] "that politely put answers give questions give perhaps the answer."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that was your point let me first find the place where I responded to the objection of Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this is page 54, line 17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is the second. But you introduced again your -- that you did not say that the witness was a representative of the -- of course, you did not repeat that at that very moment. But sometimes Mr. Piletta-Zanin, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps if I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we can have a look at page 44 line 24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The first issue, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, was on page 46 where you used the words "representative of the Prosecution." If you say that at a later stage you did not use these same words, that is perfectly correct. But not using these words does not always mean that you are showing the politeness necessary. And I can tell you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, apart from the words that you used, sometimes there are other ways, the way you use your voice can be just as -- I am not just talking about that one and only question, but it is also the general attitude, the way you did put the questions to this expert witness, the way you interrupted her, the way you treated her, all taken altogether, and then using this tone while questioning, could give the result that I indicated. I take notice that you take it that the rights of the Defence have been violated in this respect and the Chamber does.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We had not dealt with the issue of the exhibits for Ewa Tabeau, had we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We had given them a number, but we had not yet admitted them into evidence. It was on the request of the Chamber, so since the Chamber received what the Chamber would like to see, and since we thought that the best way of adding it to the report of the expert witness that, unless there is any objection at this very moment, we would make that part of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think though, Mr. President, that we had deferred dealing with all of the exhibits in respect to Ewa Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I totally agree with you, we did that. Then we are again dependent on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will go through them at a rather low pace, because especially numbers are very difficult to cope with, both for those who transcribe the hearing and for the interpreters. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P3729, CD-ROM; P3731, expert report of Ewa Tabeau --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence has an objection here. Because at the very same time that a reply was given by this person earlier, it seems to us that mathematically speaking, the conclusions of the report are faulty, partially or fully in the sense that rates were drawn which we -- since we have different figures. So rates were drawn from figures therefore, there are different figures. And if we are covering the entire period, in this sense, the report doesn't seem correct to us, doesn't seem truthful, and therefore it has to be rejected. On principle, we are always making the same observations, like the one we raised earlier, politely, and the issue of witnesses, we still believe these are elements that are coming from the Prosecution and should not be to opposed as evidence as they come from one party. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, any need to respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't think there is a need to respond. The thing is that a proper response involves a complete assessment of what the witness has just said. The witness has just said that the figures have not changed, that what she has done now is to give a breakdown of the figures that were not used in her report. Because questions have been asked about rates in respect to the period before the indictment period, that is a period outside of the study. She did that as a result of the request of the Defence and it is not that there are differences between one figure in one report, and this report. The difference is that these are new figures. She did not, in her report, examine the period before the indictment period began.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. It is -- the issue raised by you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is not an issue of admissibility and in respect of your repeated objection against I would say, testimony coming from those who are employed by the Office of the Prosecutor, the Chamber is aware of the position that the Defence takes, that, in general, that no one could take the stand who is employed by the Prosecutor. At the same time, as you might have noticed, in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence there is specific mention made of those belonging to the Office of the Prosecutor appearing as witness before a Chamber. The objection is denied. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3731.1, B/C/S translation; Exhibit P3731A addendum to expert report of Ewa Tabeau --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is only formally, but we would like to state that our position is still the same as before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. The objection is then similarly denied.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P3731B, addendum to expert report of Ewa Tabeau; P3731C, addendum to report of Ewa Tabeau; P3730, annex number one; P3730A, annex number two; D154, facts cover sheet and chart; D155, chart in B/C/S; D1551, partial translation; D156, article in B/C/S; D156.1, partial translation; D157, chart entitled "sniper from 10/09/1992 until 10/08/1994 in B/C/S; D157.1, English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, again, formally speaking, our objection relates to all the addendum of -- or the addenda of the Tabeau report. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The Prosecution objects to D156. All we have here is a figure from an article by someone unknown to the witness, and she says the figure is wrong. It is something that is not of any assistance and is not probative of anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, might we have a -- might the Chamber have a look at D156.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection will be -- is denied, but, of course, the witness has been asked questions about it. She did not agree with numbers in this article. So the probative value, I would say, at this very moment, is still rather limited, that at least someone has published at least these numbers were published and that the witness did not agree. So -- but in view of the fact that they were published, and that fact of course comes out, but just in order to give some guidance to the Defence, if the Defence would rely upon these figures as according to the truth, then, of course, the sources of these figures should be given in more detail and there would be -- we would need an opportunity at least to challenge these figures in one way or the other by the Prosecution. So I am just explaining what -- not perhaps what but that this document at this moment has a rather relative limited probative value.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank the Chamber for this and I believe that we understood that what the Defence wanted to prove is that there was kind of inflated figures here and the sources were unsure. I don't think we will go there, but thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, having gone through the documents, I take it that -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, we would be ready for the next witness but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, two minutes would not be wise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: However there is an issue we could use two minutes in. It is in respect of protective measures for a witness that is scheduled to come soon. Perhaps if we could go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we could do that. We will now turn in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Arifagic, I take it, before giving testimony in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text of this declaration will be handed out to you now by the usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. You will first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution. Please, Ms. Mahindaratne proceed?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I proceed, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please stated your full name and spell out your last name.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC
